steps.title: Five banned words
paragraphs: There's nothing wrong with these words. But they're tired: they've been used so often that readers slide right past them without seeing, hearing or feeling anything.
Today they're banned. Without them, you'll have to reach for senses, comparisons and strong verbs instead, and your writing will be better for it.

cards.title: Why ban words?
cards.body: A word like “scary” tells the reader how to feel. A banned-word challenge forces you to show it instead: the twig snapping behind you, the cold sweat on your neck. Limits like this push writers to be creative.

cards.title: Tired or vivid?
cards.telling: The very loud music was scary.
cards.showing: The bass thumped through the floor until my teeth buzzed, and every flash of light showed a different face.
cards.note: No banned words, and you can hear, feel and see it.

cards.title: Mix your tools
cards.body: In this challenge, use everything from the unit: details for at least four senses, a simile, a metaphor and some personification. Use your word bank and the comparison helper. With only 300 words, every word has to earn its place.

cards.title: Without the banned words
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that make this scene frightening without saying “scary”.
cards.text: The hallway was pitch-black, and something behind the door scratched.

prompts: Which banned word was hardest to live without? What did you use instead?
Which sentence in your scene is the most vivid, and which tools did you use in it?
